title: Satirical Rhetoric: Conditionals, Counterfactuals, and Modality

sections.title: Counterfactual Framing with 'mintha... lenne'
sections.content: Social satire exposes human folly by treating absurd illusions as if they were unquestioned reality. In Hungarian, pairing 'mintha' (as if) with conditional forms creates this theatrical distance: 'Úgy viselkedik, mintha ő irányítaná az egész várost' (He behaves as if he were directing the whole town). The particle 'szinte már-már' (virtually / bordering on) heightens this disproportion: 'Szinte már-már azt hihetnénk, hogy a gróf maga Napóleon császár.'

sections.title: Polite Irony vs. Open Mockery (gúny vs. irónia)
sections.content: While 'gúny' (mockery / sarcasm) is aggressive and divisive, authentic literary satire ('szatíra') uses polite formal phrasing and rhetorical restraint to let hypocrisy ('álszentség') defeat itself. Framing questions with 'Aligha hinné bárki, hogy...' exposes pretensions without resorting to insult.

sections.title: Satirical Discourse Structures
rows: hardly would anyone believe that... (rhetorical skepticism)

items.spanish: Úgy tesz a hivatalnok, mintha az ő engedélye nélkül megállna az élet.
items.english: The official acts as if life would stop without his permission.

items.spanish: Szinte már-már azt hihetnénk, hogy a kisvárosi vita világméretű konfliktus.
items.english: One would virtually think that the small-town dispute is a worldwide conflict.

items.spanish: A szatíra kíméletlenül leleplezi a társadalmi álszentséget és gőgöt.
items.english: Satire ruthlessly unmasks social hypocrisy and arrogance.

items.spanish: Aligha hinné bárki, hogy a gróf komolyan gondolta az ágyúlövéseket.
items.english: Hardly would anyone believe that the count was serious about the cannon shots.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: In Hungarian satire, the most damaging critiques are wrapped in impeccable formal politeness.
